content.text: {"persuasion":"UNPERSUADED","support_scope":"NONE","rationale":"The book strongly establishes that righteousness can denote actual right conduct and that grace does not abolish obedience. It does not, however, establish that right-living is the substance of every relevant use. The strongest counter-reading is context-sensitive: righteousness denotes rightness according to God, appearing as God’s just character and action, human right conduct, or a favorable standing God reckons in justification. Romans 4:5-8 decisively favors the forensic sense in its own context: God justifies the ungodly, imputes righteousness without works, forgives iniquities, and does not impute sin. The book’s wage-versus-duty distinction successfully shows that Paul is not rejecting subsequent obedience, but it does not turn this reckoned status into performed right-living.
